clue.text: A phrase circulating about lover boy

indicators.note: the phrase goes round, encircling the word for about

parts.note: a motto is a short phrase or saying
re is Latin-derived for about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone keeps repeating a saying about a young lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lover boy' sounds like a romantic young man; in art an amoretto is a winged infant, so the definition is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a little cupid figure in art, a winged boy representing love.

clue.text: They debate in the Guardian about sovereign

indicators.note: the guardian's name goes around the sovereign's letters

parts.note: Argus, the hundred-eyed giant of Greek myth, was set as a watchman or guardian
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the sovereign

explanation.surface: Debaters featured in the Guardian newspaper are discussing the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Guardian' looks like the newspaper but means the mythical hundred-eyed watchman; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: People who argue are those who debate a point.

clue.text: Issue old folios, bound together

parts.note: ff is the abbreviation for folios, pages
a bound is a leap, a spring

explanation.surface: Old pages of a book are issued, bound together in one volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' and 'bound' look like publishing words; issue means children, and bound means a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in the legal sense means children or descendants.

clue.text: Serious money put down

definitions.meaning: a deposit paid as a pledge that a bargain will be completed

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both solemnly sincere and a deposit paid to secure a deal.

clue.text: Hands over pots containing money? The opposite

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it
tells us to reverse the stated container: the money holds the pots, not the pots the money

parts.note: tin is slang for money
urns are pots or vessels

explanation.surface: Someone hands over pots full of cash, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the pots would hold the money; 'The opposite' flips that, so the money word is the one that does the holding.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in is to hand over or surrender something to authorities.

clue.text: Beginning to gulp fruit, I suppressed hiccup

indicators.note: only the opening letter of gulp is taken
the letter for I is held down and taken out of the fruit

parts.note: a litchi, or lychee, is a Chinese fruit

explanation.surface: Someone gulping fruit tries to stifle a hiccup.
explanation.walkthrough: The fruit is spelt litchi here, the older form of lychee; 'suppressed' takes out its final letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup is a minor setback or snag, much like a small fault in a system.

clue.text: Inexperienced sorceress wasting time in part of London

parts.note: green means naive, inexperienced

indicators.note: the time letter is lost, wasted away, from the sorceress

parts.note: a witch is a sorceress

explanation.surface: A novice sorceress loses track of time in a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' drops T from WITCH, leaving WICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenwich is a borough in south-east London, home of the meridian.

clue.text: Statesman, one introducing new serial

indicators.note: the numeral comes first, leading into the rest

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the letters of serial are made new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician launches a fresh serial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SERIAL to SRAELI, introduced by I.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the state of Israel can playfully be called a state's man.

clue.text: Runner, someone who'll give a damn about nothing

indicators.note: the swearer goes around the zero

parts.note: a curser is someone who swears, who says damn
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A runner who doesn't care about anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give a damn' usually means caring; here it means literally swearing, so CURSER, with O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A courser is a swift horse, a runner, and also a fast-running bird.

clue.text: Attack insurance agent, finally out to risk everything

parts.note: to go for someone is to attack them

indicators.note: the last letter is put out of the word

parts.note: an insurance broker arranges policies

explanation.surface: Lashing out at an insurance agent, someone gambles everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally out' removes the R that ends BROKER.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for broke is an idiom for staking all you have on one attempt.

clue.text: Commander outmanoeuvred visibly in this?

indicators.note: the letters can be seen sitting inside the words commander outmanoeuvred

explanation.surface: Asks what happens when a commander is clearly outwitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of 'commandeR OUTmanoeuvred', and the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing defeat, which an outmanoeuvred commander would suffer.

clue.text: Deadpan, having nothing to say

definitions.meaning: read literally, lacking expressions, phrases or utterances

explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face shows no feeling; read literally, the word means lacking any phrases to utter.

clue.text: Container for transporting heavy weight in northern town

parts.note: a skip is a large container for carrying away rubble
a ton is a heavy unit of weight

explanation.surface: A skip carries a heavy load through a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: A SKIP is a British builder's waste container (US dumpster); SKIPTON is a market town in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Skipton is a market town in North Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Supervisor's charged with this act of negligence

definitions.meaning: supervision, the watch a supervisor is responsible for
a mistake caused by failing to notice something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both supervision and a careless mistake, two nearly opposite senses.

clue.text: Copycat behaviour making .. opera character weep

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme
to cry is to weep

explanation.surface: An imitative act causes an opera heroine to burst into tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The '..' is a print artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimicry is imitation, the copying of another's behaviour.

clue.text: Awfully mad on epic books

indicators.note: the letters are treated awfully, scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is terribly keen on long epic books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges MADONEPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Compendia are comprehensive collections of information, typically books.

clue.text: Nameless hoodlum, a comedian

indicators.note: without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: a gangster is a hoodlum

explanation.surface: An anonymous thug turns out to be a stand-up comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' removes N (name) from GANGSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gagster is someone who tells gags, a joker or comedian.

clue.text: Evaders turning hostile

indicators.note: the letters of evaders turn into a new order

explanation.surface: Fugitives turn nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges EVADERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means opposing or unfavourable, close to hostile.

clue.text: Part of Africa, say, ringed by roads that are up

indicators.note: one piece is encircled by the other
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: lanes are minor roads
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A region of Africa where the roads are all dug up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'that are up' means read upwards, i.e. reversed; 'ringed by' puts the word for say inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Abysmal, like male needing elegant clothing

indicators.note: the stylish word wraps around the others like clothes

parts.note: chic means elegant
as means like

explanation.surface: A man who wants smart clothes looks dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abysmal' usually means very bad, but here it is meant literally: like an abyss.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasmic means like a chasm, so abysmal in the literal sense of being like an abyss.

clue.text: Official taking time to consider

parts.note: a consul is a government official abroad

explanation.surface: A diplomat takes time to think things over.
explanation.definitionFit: To consult is to take counsel or to consider, as in consult one's feelings.

clue.text: Welcome a call from the speaker

indicators.note: the words are what a speaker says aloud

parts.note: a call on something is a claim to it

explanation.surface: Someone shouts a greeting through the loudspeaker.
explanation.walkthrough: A CLAIM, from 'a call', said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim is to greet with enthusiasm, to welcome loudly.

clue.text: About to get order to fight "search and destroy"

parts.note: C, circa, means about
OM is the Order of Merit
a bout is a fight

explanation.surface: A commander issues the order to fight in a search-and-destroy mission.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb out is to search thoroughly and remove unwanted elements.

clue.text: .Chairman's given out a cosmetic

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: The chairman has handed out a face cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CHAIRMANSGIVEN; the stray dot is a print artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing cream is a light skin cream that leaves no greasy trace, a cosmetic.

clue.text: Broadcast supporting government leader

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: the leading letter of government

explanation.surface: A broadcast backs the head of government.
explanation.definitionFit: A prog is short for programme, a broadcast.

clue.text: Drive to skip breakfast, presumably

definitions.meaning: literally to rise and leave without eating

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means energetic drive, and literally to rise and leave straight away.

clue.text: Religious fanatic given a piece of land beyond zone's borders

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first
the first and last letters of zone form its borders

parts.note: a lot is a plot of land

explanation.surface: A fanatic is granted a plot outside the zone's limits.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is an extreme believer; the Zealots were a Jewish sect.

clue.text: Law laid down by court backing southern Florida town

indicators.note: the court comes behind, at the back of the rest

parts.note: Tampa is a city in Florida

explanation.surface: A law is enacted by a court supporting a town in southern Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stamp Act of 1765 was a British law taxing American colonies.
